Wow, just a few hours ago (yep, we finished up at midnight) we ground up (w/the kitchenaid attachment we’ve used for yrs) 7 lbs of chuck, 3 lbs for a dinner tmrw, the other 2.75 frozen for later. (1.25 came off as fat). 
Here’s the thing, now I think I maybe handled the patties a little bit too much. (No, no kneading!) Plus we salt & pepper as or before we grind. That said I’ve done this many times before and they usually come out super great. We cook them on a gas grill, so they just have to stay together a wee bit more.  They were falling apart too much once, that was not fun. 
I do 1/3 lbs, it’s a dinner party ;) Also I make the middles a bit thinner, so they don’t turn into big meatballs on the grill. 
Still, 100% freshly (or close to) ground meat is miles above buying pre-ground. It can be a pain, but it’s so so delicious.

I love to make the oklahoma smash burgers, and then when you flip them over put cheese (since the onions are bound to the burger itself) Then while your burgers are cooking, saute some mushrooms and take a second patty, and when second patty is flipped, put the mushrooms on it. And cover both with cheese. You get a burger with onions and sauteed mushrooms, but the cheese binds it and makes it a bit less messy. Plus it makes for an amazing double stack with onions integrated into one burger, and mushrooms topped on another. With the onions being on the downward facing side, and the sauteed mushrooms being covered with cheese on the upward side. Which I find works well regardless if you choose to put your lettuce, tomato, etc on the bottom burger bun or the top. I myself am a guy who puts the veggies on the bottom to give the burger some drainage.
